# Real-shape CASS oracle corpus — provenance of THIS committed tree

bd-reality-core-convergence-1azkt.43, deliverable 2. The field-by-field record
tables live beside the generator, in
[`scripts/real_shape_corpus/SHAPES.md`](../../../scripts/real_shape_corpus/SHAPES.md),
deliberately not copied here: the tables and the renderer must move together, and
a second copy is the kind that drifts. What this file records is the provenance of
the bytes actually committed under this directory.

## Exactly how to reproduce this tree

Generate into an EMPTY directory, never over this one:

    python3 scripts/real_shape_corpus/generate.py \
        --out "$(mktemp -d)" --workspace /work/ledger \
        --seed 43 --target-records 4000 --digest

To refresh the committed copy, generate into a fresh directory first, confirm the
digest, then copy the changed files across. Generating directly over this
directory cannot reproduce the digest, for the reason stated below: SHAPES.md
lives here and the generator does not write it, so it would be hashed as a stray
file. (`--workspace` and `--seed` match the generator's defaults; they are spelled
out because they are baked into every session path and therefore into the digest.)

Byte-identical for the same arguments: ids come from a seeded RNG and timestamps
from a fixed epoch, never from the clock. The digest is **blake2b-256**
(`hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=32)`, generate.py:430) over every file in the tree,
each path followed by its bytes, walked in sorted order.

bd-reality-core-convergence-1azkt.43's acceptance says "equal blake3". The
property it asks for -- the same seed yielding byte-identical output -- is what is
verified; the algorithm differs deliberately, because this generator imports only
the standard library and `hashlib` carries blake2b but not blake3. Reading blake3
literally would mean adding a third-party dependency to a script whose whole point
is that it needs none.

Verified by generating twice, to two different destinations, and comparing:

    tree digest   c846e3c4378814797a8e6af85377b3f08f43a0962f90b28575a7290fb3e2a5a6

The digest is a property of a FRESHLY GENERATED tree, so it cannot be reproduced
by hashing this directory in place: `tree_digest` hashes every file it finds and
this directory also carries SHAPES.md, which the generator does not write.
Regenerate into an empty directory to check it.

ANY JUDGMENT OR MANIFEST CHANGE MOVES THIS VALUE BY CONSTRUCTION, because
judgments.json is generated by `build_judgments` and is therefore hashed with
everything else. It moved twice on 2026-10-22 — once when five retrieval queries
that carried no distractors gained them, and again when the set was brought up to
the 40 queries the bead's deliverable 5(a) requires. When you change a judgment,
update this line and the `RECORDED_DIGEST` constant in
`tests/real_shape_corpus_shapes.rs` in the SAME commit, or the fixture and its own
determinism check disagree at every revision in between.

## Checks run against this tree before it was committed

- `generate.validate(<this dir>)` — **0 problems**. It walks every record and
  checks it against the envelope table, so the fixture cannot quietly drift into
  the "clean" one-line shapes this corpus exists to replace.
- The private-fleet-identifier predicate from `tests/fleet_identifier_guard.rs`,
  replicated over all 310 files: **0 hits** for any of its 14 banned host words,
  for `vmi<digits>` host names, and for routable IPv4 addresses. The corpus is
  authored, never copied from a private session, and this is the check that says
  so rather than the claim.

Note that the corpus DELIBERATELY contains secret-shaped strings and
instruction-like text, because redaction and prompt-injection quarantine are
among the properties measured against it. Those are authored decoys; they are
not real credentials.

## Why the scale variant is the committed form

The authored core alone is 14 sessions and 123 records. The failure this corpus
was built to measure — retrieval and pack latency going from about 1.2 s to
about 11 s — appeared at roughly 4,900 spans, so a 123-record tree cannot
reproduce it and a measuring stick that cannot reach the regime is not one.
`scripts/real_shape_corpus/SHAPES.md` described scale variants as "never
committed" until 2026-10-22; that line was written while nothing at all was
committed, and it is corrected there.

Regenerating the core alone (`--out <dir>` with no `--target-records`) remains
the right way to review the authored CONTENT, which is 14 reviewable sessions
rather than 308 recombined ones.
